keyChanges.title: FSD v14.3.5 rolls out: incremental RL polish, still no v15 path visible
keyChanges.description: On July 13, 2026 Tesla began rolling out software update 2026.20.6.6 with FSD (Supervised) v14.3.5 for HW4/AI4 vehicles (S/3/X/Y/Cybertruck). Official release notes claim: upgraded RL training stage, upgraded neural network vision encoder (rare/low-visibility, 3D geometry, traffic signs), AI compiler/runtime rewrite with MLIR claiming 20% faster reaction time, mitigated lane-biasing/tailgating, more decisive parking, better emergency-vehicle/school-bus/animal/traffic-light handling, improved temporary degradation recovery, and unified model between Actually Smart Summon, FSD, and Robotaxi. QoL features include Camera Preview while driving, FSD live indicator in the Tesla app, intervention-free distance tracking, and parking options on the map. Critical reality: this is another point-release on the v14.3.x branch — still fully Supervised (SAE L2), still requiring driver attention. TeslaFi stats at release showed only ~243 cars / ~1.9% of tracked fleet on 2026.20.6.6. Early impressions are mixed: NotATeslaApp/Zack reported fixed turn-lane twitch and better parking, while Teslarati and high-mileage tester David Moss reported 'horrible' parking (3 bad jobs in 23 min) and inconsistent speed profiles. Most importantly, there is zero public evidence of FSD v15 (the delayed 10B-parameter architectural overhaul) shipping, testing publicly, or advancing its end-2026/early-2027 target. Robotaxi scale remains explicitly blocked until v15 per Q1 2026 guidance. v14.3.5 is incremental supervised polish, not the unsupervised unlock.

positive_signals: Official OTA 2026.20.6.6 with FSD v14.3.5 confirmed across NotATeslaApp, TeslaNorth, and Teslarati
Release notes claim real stack work: RL upgrade, vision encoder upgrade, MLIR compiler rewrite (20% faster reaction)
Unified model between ASS, FSD, and Robotaxi — architectural consolidation progress
QoL: Camera Preview while driving, app FSD indicator, intervention-free distance tracking
Some early testers report fixed turn-lane steering twitch and smoother parking approaches
negative_signals: Still FSD Supervised only — no unsupervised capability, no v15, no robotaxi-grade autonomy
v15 (10B-param architectural overhaul) remains delayed to late-2026/early-2027 with no public milestone this week
Early rollout tiny: ~243 cars / ~1.9% of TeslaFi-tracked fleet at release
Mixed/regressive early feedback: Teslarati and David Moss report terrible parking jobs; speed profiles still inconsistent
Release notes list 'Upcoming Improvements' still pending (expand reasoning beyond destination handling; pothole avoidance) — core gaps acknowledged unfixed
v14.3.x is still the production ceiling while large-scale robotaxi expansion remains blocked until v15 ships

keyChanges.title: Report: HW4 consumer FSD runs distilled Cybercab models — hardware tiering confirmed
keyChanges.description: On July 14, 2026 NotATeslaApp published an exclusive claiming Tesla develops FSD models first for Cybercab's more powerful FSD hardware, then distills them into smaller 'student' models for consumer HW4/AI4 vehicles — analogous to how FSD v14 Lite is a distilled v14 for HW3. The report argues this is good news for HW4 unsupervised hopes (HW4 still in the running, unlike HW3 which is permanently capped), because consumer cars receive optimized versions of the same robotaxi stack. Critical read: this is a single-source exclusive citing an unnamed source — confidence is low until corroborated. If true, it confirms a multi-tier capability hierarchy (Cybercab native > HW4 distilled > HW3 Lite ceiling) and implies consumer HW4 may never run the full-weight teacher model that Cybercab gets. Combined with the confirmed v15 delay and Cybercab-first development, it reinforces that unsupervised consumer FSD depends on distillation quality, not parity with robotaxi hardware. No official Tesla confirmation.

positive_signals: If accurate, HW4 remains on the unsupervised path (unlike HW3, which Tesla confirmed cannot do unsupervised FSD)
Cybercab-first development with distillation is a rational engineering path for multi-hardware fleets
Consistent with known v14 Lite distillation pattern for HW3
negative_signals: Single-source exclusive (NotATeslaApp) with unnamed source — no Tesla confirmation, no Teslarati/TeslaNorth corroboration
Implies consumer HW4 gets second-class/lighter models vs Cybercab native stack
Does not advance v15 ship date; distillation is process, not a capability milestone
Reinforces hardware tiering: Cybercab > HW4 distilled > HW3 Lite (permanent unsupervised exclusion for ~4M HW3 vehicles)
Vague on how much capability is lost in distillation — no metrics on student vs teacher performance gap

keyChanges.title: HW3 FSD v14 Lite completes claimed 4,255-mile zero-intervention coast-to-coast drive
keyChanges.description: On July 17, 2026 TeslaNorth reported that drivers Koby Pierce and 'Liam's Dad' completed a diagonal US coast-to-coast run (Key West, FL to Cape Flattery, WA — 4,255 miles) in a 2020 Model 3 Long Range (HW3, 175k+ miles) on FSD v14 Lite, claiming zero manual steering, braking, accelerator, or turn-signal inputs. The trip is part of a larger 'Buoy to Bay' expedition. Critical reality: this is a self-reported enthusiast demonstration, not an independent audit. Drivers remained in the vehicle (Supervised), so SAE L2 supervision was still present even if hands-off. HW3 remains officially capped at v14 Lite with no path to unsupervised FSD or v15 (confirmed Q1 2026). A successful supervised long-haul does not change the permanent hardware ceiling for ~4 million HW3 vehicles, nor does it substitute for the delayed v15 architectural upgrade needed for robotaxi scale. Treat as positive signal for v14 Lite highway reliability, not as unsupervised readiness.

positive_signals: Self-reported 4,255-mile diagonal US crossing on HW3 FSD v14 Lite with zero claimed interventions
High-mileage (175k+) 2020 Model 3 LR — stress test on older hardware and battery
Corroborates that v14 Lite can handle long-haul highway/intercity supervised driving on HW3
negative_signals: Self-reported enthusiast claim — no independent third-party audit of intervention logs
Still Supervised: drivers present; SAE L2, not unsupervised autonomy
HW3 permanently excluded from unsupervised FSD and v15 (official Q1 2026 confirmation)
v14 Lite remains the 'ultimate ceiling' for HW3 — no software path past this
Does not move the v15 timeline or robotaxi scale blocker

keyChanges.title: FSD fleet hits 12 billion cumulative supervised miles; training data grows, software still on v14
keyChanges.description: As of ~July 17, 2026 Tesla FSD (Supervised) fleet miles surpassed 12 billion globally, roughly one month after the 11 billion mark (June 9). Community tracking cited by TeslaNorth estimates 26–30 million new miles per day, with >4.5 billion of the total on city streets. Europe contributed 50M+ km across five small approved markets. Critical framing for the software roadmap: data volume continues to accelerate and feeds RL hard-example mining (explicitly referenced in v14.3.5 release notes for traffic lights, rare objects, animals). But cumulative miles are not a substitute for the delayed v15 10B-parameter architectural overhaul. Tesla has already stated current v14 is not safe enough for large-scale robotaxi expansion without 'major architectural improvements' — more supervised miles improve the current model but do not ship the next architecture. Metric is community-tracked, not an official Tesla IR disclosure.

positive_signals: 12B cumulative FSD Supervised miles (~1B added in ~5 weeks from 11B on June 9)
Daily accumulation estimated at 26–30M miles/day — rapid data flywheel
>4.5B miles on city streets — hardest domain for end-to-end driving
v14.3.5 release notes explicitly credit fleet-sourced hard RL examples for traffic lights, rare objects, animals
negative_signals: All 12B miles are Supervised (L2) — not unsupervised robotaxi miles
More data does not ship v15; architecture delay to late-2026/early-2027 remains the blocker
Community-tracked metric, not official Tesla IR audited disclosure
Musk previously admitted current stack needs major architectural improvements for scale safety
Europe's contribution (~50M km ≈ 31M miles) is a rounding error vs global total

metricUpdate.note: FSD (Supervised) cumulative fleet miles globally surpassed 12 billion (~26-30M miles/day; >4.5B city streets). Community-tracked, not official IR. Production software remains FSD v14.3.5 (Supervised); v15 still targeted late-2026/early-2027.
